title: Laminar live report v1
description: An outcome report from someone who ran quotes against a live venue. It carries CONCLUSIONS the reporter computed locally, never the market data those conclusions were computed from. `additionalProperties` is false throughout, so a field that is not listed here cannot be submitted — that is the mechanism, not a style choice. See docs/FEEDBACK_PROTOCOL.md.

reported_at.description: Date the report was written, ISO 8601.

reporter.description: GitHub handle or any pseudonym you like, for credit. Optional — an anonymous report is still worth having. Do not put an e-mail address here; the leak scan rejects them.

laminar_commit.description: The Laminar commit you ran. Without it a disagreement cannot be attributed.

venue.description: Only Polymarket is modelled. A report from another venue would need its own scoring rules.

epochs.description: Number of reward epochs the report aggregates. One is enough to be useful.

observations.description: One entry per thing you measured. Mixed kinds are fine.

notes.description: Free text: caveats, what went wrong, what you would not trust in your own numbers. Prose only — do not paste data here.

verdict.description: Where the realised quantity fell relative to Laminar's predicted interval. `undetermined` is a first-class answer — house rule 2 is that you count what you cannot resolve rather than defaulting it.

condition_id.description: Public market condition_id. 64 hex characters — a 40-character wallet address cannot satisfy this pattern, deliberately. Optional; omit it if naming the market tells anyone too much about your position.

denominator_measurement.title: Q4 — the reward denominator, measured rather than bracketed
denominator_measurement.description: The highest-value report. Your realised share of a reward pool is a direct measurement of the competing field's total score D, which is never published. Requires no market data: mine_qmin comes from your own order log through src/laminar/score.py, the other two come off your own reward statement.

mine_qmin.description: YOUR score, summed over the same samples the reward covers, from laminar.score.qmin().

reward_paid_usdc.description: What you were actually paid over those epochs.

pool_usdc.description: The advertised pool over those epochs (daily_rate x days). See the protocol doc on why an under-distributed pool biases d_implied upward.

d_implied.description: mine_qmin * (pool_usdc - reward_paid_usdc) / reward_paid_usdc. CI recomputes this from your inputs and rejects the report if it disagrees by more than 0.5%.

d_min.description: Lower bracket from laminar.score.denominator_bounds() on the book you observed.

d_max.description: Upper bracket from the same call.

queue_bracket.title: Q1/Q5 — did real fills land inside the front/back-of-queue bracket
queue_bracket.description: shadow.py claims the truth lies between QUEUE_FRONT and QUEUE_BACK. Live fills test that claim. A `below` verdict — fewer real fills than the pessimistic bound — falsifies it.

orders_resting.description: Orders you rested that shadow.py was also asked to simulate.

orders_filled.description: How many actually filled, wholly or partly.

predicted_fills_back.description: shadow.replay(queue=QUEUE_BACK) on the same orders — the pessimistic bound.

unresolved.description: Cases the simulator declined to decide. Report it; it is the honest part of the output.

yield_realised.title: The headline — did realised reward yield land in the predicted interval
yield_realised.description: Gross reward yield only. Do not net out adverse selection here; report that separately as `other`, because Laminar has no prediction to compare it against yet.

capital_usdc.description: Capital actually committed to resting quotes, averaged over the window.

other.title: Anything the three kinds above cannot express
other.description: An escape hatch on purpose. If you measured something real and the schema has no shape for it, say so in prose rather than forcing it into the wrong field — a wrong field is worse than free text.

question.description: Which docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md item this bears on.

summary.description: What you measured, how, and what you concluded. Prose and summary statistics — not data.
